//: Local to this node, not shared on the CSV: copy to C:\ProgramData\HyperVCsiAgent\agent.config.json (the default path - no --config needed) so a config change can be edited on one node and piloted by failing the clustered role over onto it before touching the other node. The installer normally writes this file for you.

Agent.//Snapshots: A snapshot is a full VHDX copy, so it lives in its own directory and on its own clock. The copy runs for as long as the CSV takes - hours for a large disk on a volume that cannot block-clone - which is why the timeout is measured in hours rather than in DiskOperationTimeout's minutes, and why concurrent copies are capped separately: a few of them must never be able to wedge every CreateVolume on the agent.
Agent.//HostOperations: Attaching a disk goes through the Hyper-V host that currently owns the node's VM. Bounded per host, and on a shorter clock than disk operations because none of it is bulk I/O.
Agent.//Tls: The server certificate is self-signed, the same as the driver's client certificate, so it is pinned by thumbprint rather than validated against a CA. HostName is a separate check: Kestrel's host filtering rejects any caller not addressing the agent by this name, independent of which certificate they trust. The store is re-read every ReloadInterval, so installing a new certificate and adding its thumbprint here is picked up without restarting the clustered role.
Agent.//Authentication: Fingerprints of the self-signed client certificates allowed to call this agent. The matching key lives in a Kubernetes Secret mounted into the CSI controller. List two during a rotation - add the new one, roll the driver, then remove the old.
